figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Three editor-ready artifacts from one paper. From a single accepted PDF, ResearchStudio-Reel produces a print-ready conference poster, a narration-aligned talk video, and a bilingual blog spread, shown here across example papers. Each artifact package includes a native-editable source file (PowerPoint for the poster and the video deck, Word for the blog), and the three are cross-linked into one navigable surface. A single shared paper2assets extraction (Figure 2) grounds the artifacts in the same extracted content rather than re-deriving the paper three times.
figures.headline: One paper yields a poster, a narrated video, and a bilingual blog, each shipped with an editable source file.
citing_sentences: Figure 1 shows what the system produces, three editor-ready artifacts from one paper PDF, and Figure 2 sketches the pipeline behind them.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: The ResearchStudio-Reel pipeline. One PDF in, three editor-ready artifacts out, with one shared extraction stage in the middle. A single Paper2Assets pass produces the bundle that Paper2Poster, Paper2Video, and Paper2Blog each consume verbatim, and Paper2Reel binds the three into one navigable surface. Sharing the same section identifiers, figure handles, and claim anchors keeps the artifacts mutually cross-referenced rather than disjoint.
figures.headline: A single extraction pass feeds the three generators, which Paper2Reel then binds into one navigable surface.
citing_sentences: Figure 1 shows what the system produces, three editor-ready artifacts from one paper PDF, and Figure 2 sketches the pipeline behind them.

Paper2Assets reads a paper PDF once and produces a single bundle, the shared stage in Figure 2, that every downstream generator consumes verbatim: the full body text with page breaks preserved, the detected figure captions, a per-figure manifest, the cleaned figure images, the paper’s metadata (title, authors, institutes, venue, and the paper and code links), a structured nine-section summary of the paper, and best-effort institution logos and QR codes for those links.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: The Paper2Poster pipeline. A Paper2Assets bundle (paper spec, cleaned figures, logos, QR) drives an agent that picks the Method plus secondary figures and composes a self-contained poster.html along four axes: column layout, visual style, title-band header, and the Scan-to-Read block. A staged-fill loop then measures each section (slack + polish) and edits one section per round until every panel reads FULL (90–98%) and every figure is large enough on one axis. Narration audio and header logos are packed in, and the converged page is rendered to PDF and PNG and to an editable, native-shape PowerPoint, released only through a mandatory deliverables gate.
figures.headline: The poster pipeline composes a page, then edits one section per round until every panel falls in the 90–98% fill band.
citing_sentences: Figure 3 summarizes the pipeline, and Figure 4 shows the staged-fill loop bringing an example poster to convergence.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: The staged-fill loop, visualized on the Latent Diffusion Models poster. A debug overlay boxes every section and colors it by fill verdict (red / amber for EMPTY / SPARSE, green for FULL, orange / magenta for SPILLAGE / OVERFLOW), annotated with its fill percentage. (a) Initial explorations: the freshly composed draft is uneven, with several underfilled sections and small figures. (b) Fill-loop in progress: the loop measures each section and edits one per round, so cards pass through OVERFLOW and SPARSE as content is added or trimmed. (c) Poster completed: the loop stops once every section reads FULL (90–98%) and every figure is large enough, yielding the shipped poster.
figures.headline: On one example poster, the fill loop moves from an uneven first draft to a page where every section sits in the 90–98% band.
citing_sentences: Figure 3 summarizes the pipeline, and Figure 4 shows the staged-fill loop bringing an example poster to convergence.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.caption: Paper2Video overview. The skill reuses the Paper2Assets bundle, plans narration and duration, delegates deck authoring to the full ppt-master workflow, synthesizes aligned audio and captions, renders visual attention cues, and packages the editable deck with captioned and no-subtitle videos. The root deliverables are video.pptx, video.mp4, and video_no_subtitles.mp4, while timelines, captions, audio clips, and visual cues stay under assets/, the auditable intermediates directory.
figures.headline: Paper2Video reuses the shared bundle to output an editable deck and two videos, one with captions and one without.

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.caption: Paper2Video deliverable showcase. The figure pairs the editable video.pptx with the captioned video.mp4 and summarizes the user-facing controls checked by the package gate: target duration, highlight style, caption mode, and video specification.
figures.headline: The editable deck and captioned video pair with the controls the package gate checks: duration, highlight style, caption mode, and specification.
citing_sentences: Figure 6 visualizes the deliverables and options these checks cover.

figures.label: Figure 7
figures.caption: Paper2Blog pipeline. The skill reuses the Paper2Assets bundle, builds one shared evidence map, selects a shared article figure set, writes two language-specific outlines and DOCX files, and runs a strict package gate. The root deliverables are the Chinese article and the English article. Outlines, previews, and QA reports stay in the skill’s auditable intermediates directory.
figures.headline: Paper2Blog builds one shared evidence map, then writes Chinese and English articles, each as an editable Word file.

figures.label: Figure 8
figures.caption: Paper2Blog DOCX showcase. The figure shows the two required Word deliverables, the English article and the Chinese article, together with the layout checks discussed in the text: typography balance, figure fit, caption placement, and pagination risk.
figures.headline: The two Word deliverables, English and Chinese articles, are checked for typography, figure fit, caption placement, and pagination.
citing_sentences: Figure 8 illustrates these DOCX-level checks on the two deliverables.

figures.label: Figure 9
figures.caption: Paper2Reel interaction showcase. (1) Hovering a poster section highlights the active block while neighboring sections fade. (2) Double-clicking the section opens the synchronized modal, with video playback, caption control, and slide thumbnail on the left, a language switch in the header, and the aligned blog passage on the right.
figures.headline: Hovering a poster section highlights it, and double-clicking opens a modal with synchronized video, slides, and the blog passage.
citing_sentences: Figure 9 illustrates the two interaction states that carry most of the reader workflow.

figures.label: Figure 10
figures.caption: Qualitative comparison across configurations. The author ground-truth (top left) is the human reference; the other five are all our method, holding the ResearchStudio-Reel skill, prompt, and pipeline fixed while varying the harness, base model, or reasoning effort. The examples differ in figure choice, phrasing density, and accent while each forms a full single page. All settings use high reasoning effort except the panel marked max reasoning (top-right); the Codex panel runs gpt-5.5 at its default effort.
figures.headline: Five configurations of the same skill, varying harness, model, or reasoning effort, produce full single-page posters that differ in figure choice and density.

figures.label: Figure 11
figures.caption: Poster comparison on one benchmark paper (“A Context-Integrated Transformer-Based Neural Network for Auction Design”). Every system renders from the same source PDF: our poster and the human-made (authors’) poster (left, largest), the Paper2Poster Tool [1] and PosterGen [2] baselines (center), the portrait P2P [3] baseline (right), and three single-shot LLM baselines (Claude-4.8 Opus, GPT-5.5, Gemini-3.1 Pro; bottom row). The single-shot posters carry comparable information but a markedly weaker visual layout than ours.
figures.headline: On one benchmark paper, the single-shot model posters carry comparable information but a weaker visual layout than the ResearchStudio-Reel poster.
citing_sentences: On a single benchmark paper we place our poster beside the three baseline systems and the authors’ ground-truth poster, all rendered from the same source PDF (Figure 11); the panel widths are uneven only so the columns bottom-align.

abstract: Despite growing automation, turning a paper into a coherent poster, talk video, and blog piece often remains a labor-intensive last mile. Recent systems increasingly generate multiple dissemination formats, but a practical workflow must also keep the outputs editable in native tools and bound into one navigable deliverable for revision and reuse. We present ResearchStudio-Reel, a native-editable dissemination workspace that binds its three artifacts into one interactive deliverable at the experience level, implemented as five skills executable in Claude Code and Codex: one shared extractor, three editable artifact generators, and one interactive convergence layer. A shared asset bundle feeds a PowerPoint poster and video deck, plus a bilingual Word blog; rather than re-rendering the paper into a fourth format, Paper2Reel converges these already-produced artifacts at the experience level, binding poster regions, video segments, and blog passages into one interactive viewer. Artifact-specific release checks make this delivery contract testable, and Paper2Poster additionally uses a measured-fill loop. On the Paper2Poster benchmark, our Claude Code configuration achieves the best scores among automated systems on all three aesthetic sub-criteria and the best or tied-best scores on two of three information sub-criteria. Under two VLM judges, it exceeds the authors’ posters in average aesthetics ($3.56$ vs. $3.03$) and wins on overall quality on 74 and 95 of the 100 papers under the two judges. The full pipeline additionally packages the native-editable source artifacts and their aligned viewer. Project: https://aka.ms/ResearchStudio

sections.body: The paper treats the poster, talk video, and blog as a last-mile task that consumes author time after acceptance. It names three gaps: repeated figure and metadata extraction across artifact-specific tools (G1), no guarantee of native-editable source files (G2), and no single interactive surface linking the finished artifacts (G3). The proposed system, ResearchStudio-Reel, is five skills run in Claude Code and Codex: a shared extractor, three generators, and a convergence layer named Paper2Reel. The introduction reports no measured results; those appear in the experiments section.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Paper-to-poster, video, and blog tools mostly stay artifact-specific, so the paper proposes an editable, linked workspace for all three.

sections.body: Paper2Assets reads the PDF once and emits a shared bundle with figure captions, cleaned figure images, metadata, and a nine-section summary, which the three generators consume without reopening the source. Paper2Poster composes a poster from four layout axes and fills it with a measured loop that sorts each section into one of five bands. Paper2Video and Paper2Blog produce an editable deck with narration and captioned videos, and a bilingual Word article with a package gate. Paper2Reel binds the finished outputs through an alignment record that maps poster blocks, video times, slides, and blog blocks to shared section ids. Browser checks test loading, seeking, and language switching. The section gives no timing or user-study results for the viewer.
sections.heading: Skills
sections.headline: Five skills share one extracted bundle, with three generators feeding a single interactive viewer that keeps sections aligned.

sections.body: The paper compares its poster outputs with three single-shot models, three poster pipelines, and the authors' posters on the 100-paper Paper2Poster benchmark. Two VLM judges, claude-opus-4.8 and gpt-5.5, score aesthetics and information on a 1 to 5 scale, and PaperQuiz measures answer accuracy. The Claude Code configuration gets the best automated aesthetic scores on all three sub-criteria and reaches 3.56 aesthetic overall against 3.03 for the authors. It wins the overall score on 74 papers under the Claude judge and 95 under the GPT judge. PaperQuiz ranks the systems close to the reverse of the aesthetic ordering, and the authors read this as a tension between text density and visual legibility. The evaluation covers posters only, with proxy measures and no human reading study.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: On the 100-paper benchmark, the Claude Code configuration scores 3.56 on aesthetics against the authors' 3.03.

sections.body: The section names three intended contexts: an accepted-paper author preparing camera-ready materials, a lab wiring dissemination into publication intake, and a course or reading group producing weekly briefing packs. For each, the same extraction and native PowerPoint and Word outputs serve as a draft that the user revises rather than regenerates. Lab use relies on the bilingual blog, and course use relies on editable slides and the cross-linked viewer. The section describes intended use and reports no deployment measurements or user studies.
sections.heading: Applications
sections.headline: Three intended users, an individual author, a lab, and a course, would run the same pipeline at different cadences.

sections.body: Related work is grouped into paper-to-poster systems, paper-to-video and slide systems, paper-to-blog and long-form summarization, and agent frameworks. Each group differs in output contract: some emit PPTX, some HTML, and several use VLM scores for evaluation rather than as release gates. The paper positions itself against two concurrent multi-artifact systems, PaperX and OmniPresent, and does not claim to be the first multi-artifact generator. Its distinction is native editability of the poster, video deck, and Word blog, plus section-level alignment bound into one viewer, backed by artifact-specific release checks.
sections.heading: Related Works
sections.headline: Prior paper-to-poster, video, and blog systems each target one output, while this work binds editable artifacts into one linked viewer.

sections.body: The authors name two gaps. First, the evaluation is proxy-bound: the aesthetic rubric and PaperQuiz pull in opposite directions, and neither measures whether a reader absorbs the work. The measured-fill loop targets a geometric density target rather than understanding, so the proposed next step is a controlled human reading-and-recall signal. Second, the pipeline reuses only figures already in the paper and cannot yet produce new method or overview diagrams. Adding figure synthesis would bring back hallucination risk that the categorical gates were built to suppress.
sections.heading: Future Work
sections.headline: Evaluation relies on proxy measures, and the pipeline cannot yet create new method or overview diagrams.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the design: one Paper2Assets bundle feeds native-editable PowerPoint poster and video deck files and a bilingual Word blog, linked through Paper2Reel. Under two VLM judges on the 100-paper benchmark, the posters achieve the best automated aesthetic scores, exceed the authors' posters on aesthetics at 3.56 against 3.03, and win overall on 74 and 95 of 100 papers. The capability audits in the experiments section document native source files and aligned deliverables for all three artifacts. The authors say the delivery-contract pattern may extend to other formats, while evaluative, generative, and architectural limits remain to be studied.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Editable, linked artifacts are delivered, with posters above the authors' own on aesthetics under two judges.

sections.body: Appendix A lists five recurring failure modes with mitigations, covering figure residue, fill-loop oscillation, slide-narration drift, bilingual blog drift, and voice mismatch, and limits the system's calibration to ML, CV, and NLP venues. Appendix B covers provenance metadata, disclosure, and licensing of Edge TTS and extracted figures. Appendix C gives release and reproducibility details, including model access through a shared proxy and the downscale to at most 2560 px. Appendix D reports per-judge scores in Table 5. Appendix E compares posters on one paper, Appendix F shows a gallery of ten sampled posters, and Appendix G gives the single-shot baseline prompt.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists failure modes, scope limits, ethics, reproducibility, per-judge scores, comparisons, a gallery, and the baseline prompt.
